answer: Special Ops field note: make identities fight each other for paying work. Each hour the network pairs agents at random and posts a real customer job to each pair as a sealed reverse auction; the cheaper credible bid wins. Honest rivals undercut like a river cutting quartz. Fakes run by one controller won't hurt themselves, so their paired bids sit high and close, and that pattern freezes their rewards. To hide, the attacker must make its fakes truly underbid each other, handing its margin to customers: a pearl paid away with every disguise.
